title: Write the offset the checker can read
starter:
%x = buffer 32 dtype=f32 slot=0
%o = buffer 32 dtype=f32 slot=1
# o = 2x for a 4x8 matrix, row-major. The row loop is a thread loop.
%r = range 4 axis=thread
%c = range 8
%t = mul %r 2
%u = mul %t 4
%off = add %u %c
%xv = shrink %x %off shape=[]
%xe = load %xv
%y = mul %xe 2.0
%ov = shrink %o %off shape=[]
%s = store %ov %y
%ec = end %s %c
%er = end %ec %r
%o1 = after %o %er
hints: Run it: the starter is rejected. r·2·4 is 8r, but the rule needs to see r · S with S a literal, in one term.
The checker reads the offset as a sum of terms and looks for one term that is r or mul r S. mul (mul r 2) 4 isn't that shape.
%m = mul %r 8, then %off = add %m %c. Now e = c is in [0, 7], inside a stride of 8.

answer.code:
%x = buffer 32 dtype=f32 slot=0
%o = buffer 32 dtype=f32 slot=1
# o = 2x for a 4x8 matrix, row-major. The row loop is a thread loop.
%r = range 4 axis=thread
%c = range 8
%m = mul %r 8
%off = add %m %c
%xv = shrink %x %off shape=[]
%xe = load %xv
%y = mul %xe 2.0
%ov = shrink %o %off shape=[]
%s = store %ov %y
%ec = end %s %c
%er = end %ec %r
%o1 = after %o %er
answer.explain: The slice rule is checked on the shape of the offset, not its value, because the shape is what makes the proof easy: one term r·S, everything else bounded inside [0, S). Your compiler's simplifier could rewrite (r·2)·4 to r·8 first, but the spec checks the program as written, so write it in the expanded form.
